documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, can I get 90-day supplies of the levothyroxine and doxazosin sent to my pharmacy? Insurance says it's cheaper. Thanks, Dan

documents.title: RE: Refill request

documents.body: Done, 90-day supplies of both with refills went to your pharmacy. Your tenofovir stays with GI.

documents.title: Office Visit - Hypertension
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BP follow-up. Doing well. Home average about 132/84. No orthostatic symptoms on doxazosin. No spells. 

Meds: levothyroxine 125 mcg daily, doxazosin 4 mg daily, tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg daily.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P: Hypertension controlled enough on doxazosin 4 mg; continue. BMP today. Physical in the fall.

documents.title: Endocrinology Surveillance Visit
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology yearly visit, 6/14/2022. MEN2A, s/p left adrenalectomy (pheochromocytoma) and total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection (medullary carcinoma, node negative) in 2021.

One year from surgery. No palpitations, headaches or sweats. Voice normal. Weight stable. Feels well.

Labs: calcitonin remains undetectable. Plasma free metanephrines normal. TSH in range on levothyroxine 125 mcg. Calcium normal.

Plan: no change from our side. Same panel in a year, sooner for spells, a neck lump or diarrhea.
Endocrinology

reports.text: Indication: chronic hepatitis B, surveillance. Liver 15.2 cm, normal echotexture, smooth contour, no focal lesion. Portal vein patent with normal flow direction. Gallbladder without stones or wall thickening. Common bile duct 3 mm. Right kidney normal. Pancreas partially seen, unremarkable. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Normal liver; no focal hepatic lesion.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GI yearly, 7/19/2022. Taking tenofovir alafenamide every day. No complaints.

Ultrasound 7/12: normal liver, no focal lesion. HBV DNA not detected; ALT normal, albumin normal.

Plan: continue tenofovir. Return in a year with ultrasound and labs. Reminded him never to stop it without talking to us.
Gastroenterology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Age 40, yearly exam. No new concerns. Endocrinology in June: calcitonin still undetectable. GI in July: hep B suppressed, ultrasound normal. Sleeping fine, work busy but manageable.

Meds: levothyroxine 125 mcg daily, doxazosin 4 mg daily, tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg daily. Allergies: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis), latex (contact dermatitis).

Exam: vitals reviewed, BP fine. Well. Neck scar well healed, no masses. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly. No edema. Skin normal.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P:
1. HTN: at goal on doxazosin.
2. MEN2A post-resection: per endo.
3. Chronic HBV on tenofovir: per GI.
4. Mother has diabetes: A1c with today's CMP and CBC.
5. Flu and bivalent COVID boosters today, opposite arms.
No colon screening yet (starts at 45).

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All normal: A1c is in the non-diabetic range, kidney function and calcium are normal, and your blood count is fine. See you in the spring for a BP check.

documents.title: Pharmacy - prior authorization

documents.body: Pharmacy says Vemlidy needs a renewed prior authorization. Forwarded to the GI office, which prescribes it; they confirmed they will submit today. Let patient know by voicemail.

documents.body: Hi Daniel, the GI office let us know you missed your July visit and ultrasound. Those checks matter with hepatitis B, especially the yearly ultrasound. Could you call them to rebook?

documents.title: RE: Your liver follow-up
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sorry, work has been crazy. I'll call them.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth daily with breakfast; rheumatology to taper

reports.text: CT angiography of the abdomen with arterial and portal venous phase imaging and multiplanar reconstructions. Multiple small aneurysms along branches of the superior mesenteric artery with segmental areas of narrowing. Celiac axis and inferior mesenteric artery origins patent. No bowel wall thickening or pneumatosis. No active extravasation. Liver, spleen and pancreas unremarkable. Postsurgical absence of the left adrenal gland. Kidneys enhance symmetrically. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Multiple small mesenteric branch aneurysms with segmental narrowing, consistent with a medium-vessel vasculitis such as polyarteritis nodosa.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency department, 12/19/2023, arrival 19:40.

41-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B and MEN2A (s/p adrenalectomy and thyroidectomy 2021) presenting with two weeks of steadily worse fatigue, generalized weakness and vague abdominal discomfort. Low-grade fevers at home. Has lost about 4 kg in the past month without trying. Urine has looked dark for several days. On questioning, he stopped his tenofovir around May because he felt fine and kept meaning to see GI.

Meds: levothyroxine 125 mcg, doxazosin 4 mg, tenofovir (not taking since spring). Allergies: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis), latex (contact dermatitis).

Triage: BP 168/94, T 37.9 C (100.2 F), HR 98, SpO2 98% RA.
Exam: tired appearing. No rash, no joint swelling or deformity. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mildly tender in the right flank, no guarding. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.

Results: creatinine 1.64 (normal in 2022), hemoglobin 11.6 with MCV 88, ESR 68. Urinalysis: blood 2+, 15 RBC/hpf, protein negative.

Impression: subacute systemic illness with renal involvement, elevated inflammatory markers and anemia in a man with untreated hepatitis B; concern for hepatitis B related vasculitis. Admitted to medicine; ANCA, HBV DNA and mesenteric CT angiography requested.
Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Medicine
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admitted 12/19/2023 through the ED, discharged 12/23/2023.

Diagnosis: polyarteritis nodosa associated with chronic hepatitis B, with renal involvement and acute kidney injury.

Course: ANCA negative. HBV DNA 1,900,000 IU/mL off therapy. Mesenteric CT angiogram 12/20: multiple small branch aneurysms with segmental narrowing, consistent with PAN. Rheumatology and hepatology consulted. Tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg daily restarted 12/20. Prednisone 40 mg daily started 12/20. Fevers settled within two days. Creatinine 1.52 on 12/22. BP 140s-150s/90.

Discharge medications: prednisone 40 mg daily (new, rheumatology to taper), tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg daily (resumed; do not stop), doxazosin 4 mg daily, levothyroxine 125 mcg daily.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis), latex (contact dermatitis).

Follow-up: PCP within one week with BMP and CBC; rheumatology early January; GI/hepatology in about 6 weeks with HBV DNA.
Hospital Medicine

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen five days after discharge. Admitted 12/19-12/23 with hepatitis B associated polyarteritis nodosa (mesenteric CT angiogram with small aneurysms, ANCA negative, HBV DNA 1.9 million off tenofovir), with kidney involvement, creatinine 1.64 peaking, 1.52 at discharge.

He tells me he stopped the tenofovir himself around May, and that he skipped his GI visit and the physical here. He knows now. Back on tenofovir since the hospital, plus prednisone 40 mg. Fevers gone. Still tired. Appetite returning. Sleeping poorly on the steroid. Urine looks normal now.

Meds reconciled: prednisone 40 mg daily, tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg daily, doxazosin 4 mg daily, levothyroxine 125 mcg daily.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis), latex (contact dermatitis).

Exam: BP 146/92. Afebrile. Thin, tired. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, slight right flank tenderness. No rash. No edema.

A/P:
1. Polyarteritis nodosa, hepatitis B associated: rheumatology 1/9. Prednisone 40 mg until they taper. BMP and CBC today.
2. Chronic hepatitis B: tenofovir restarted; GI follow-up being rebooked, he says he will go. Discussed plainly that stopping it likely set this off.
3. Hypertension: above goal today, on steroid and with kidney involvement. Keep doxazosin, home log, recheck at next visit.
4. Sleep on prednisone: take it early in the morning.
Follow up after rheumatology, sooner for fever, flank pain or dark urine.
